item.title: Kevin Mandia’s new ‘agent swarm’ security startup Armadin raises $255.5M at $2.5B valuation
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Kevin Mandia, best known as the founder of Mandiant, has a new startup that is using agent swarms to test and protect enterprises.

item.title: Photon held a funeral for mobile apps. Now it has $4.5M to help replace them with agents.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The startup helps developers build AI agents that work over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email, and other messaging platforms. It's a bet that consumers will increasingly use agents instead of downloading apps.

item.title: Valor, Atreides, and Sequoia back AI startup Flow Engineering at $750M valuation
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Flow Engineering, which is bringing AI agents to hardware design, also landed Roelof Botha as an angel investor and board member.

item.title: Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: VC Chris Degnan and former board adviser to Factory AI has taken a job as chief revenue officer for competitor Cognition -- and everyone is arguing on X about it.

item.title: Is Neko Health’s body scan worth it? Spotify billionaire’s startup has come to America
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: Spotify founder Daniel Ek’s Neko Health raised $700 million to build a business around scanning your body, but it’s not the only company centering its roadmap around a new kind of preventative healthcare. Midjourney is building its own body scanner, while Function Health has also raised significant capital to build out its preventative-health platform. item.title: Cerebras Systems’ Andrew Feldman on whether AI can keep scaling at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman will explore the growing demand for compute, energy, and infrastructure, how Cerebras is approaching those constraints differently, and what comes next if today’s AI hardware reaches its limits.

item.title: Restate lands $20M as the need for durable infrastructure increases with AI agents
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Instead of building its durable execution engine on top of an external database, the company developed its own storage, replication, and redundancy layers. This architecture allows Restate to be exceptionally fast and lightweight.

item.title: Charter Space raises $5M to bring insurance to the stars
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: As Charter explains on its website, a common experience for space companies is that regular insurers "heard a bunch of scary science words and freaked out."

item.title: After losing his voice to cancer, this founder is building ‘glasses for voice’
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Uhura Bionics, part of the Startup Battlefield 200 at TechCrunch Disrupt, wants to replace flat, robotics voice devices with one that carries emotions.

item.title: With Dazzle, Marissa Mayer bets your camera roll has more info on your life than your inbox
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Mayer argues that if a photo is worth a thousand words, your camera roll is worth millions. By analyzing all the photos stored on your phone, Dazzle claims to understand your hobbies, interests, food, and style preferences, how you like to spend their time, and with whom.
